proposals.before: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, together with He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si he became all attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, and to each was added chief commandant of carriage escort.
proposals.after: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, together with He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si he became attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, and to each was added chief commandant of carriage escort.
proposals.reason: The literal English inserts ungrammatical “became all attendant”; 俱為 marks that the four men jointly received the office, not a title “all attendant”.

proposals.before: Yu had old ties with Hao; vulgar gentlemen, bearing encroachment, said Fan belittled himself.
proposals.after: Yu had old ties with Hao; vulgar gentlemen, nursing slights, said Fan held him cheap.
proposals.reason: 自輕 here is the charge that Wang Fan looked down on Wan Yu, not that Fan belittled himself; 挾侵 is bearing a grudge, not “bearing encroachment”.

proposals.before: Moreover secretariat aide Chen Sheng was Hao's favored minister and repeatedly slandered and ruined Fan.
proposals.after: Moreover secretariat aide Chen Sheng was Hao's favored minister and repeatedly slandered and defamed Fan.
proposals.reason: 譖毀 is repeated slander and defamation; the Chinese does not yet state that Chen Sheng succeeded in ruining Wang Fan.

proposals.before: He who loses purity then has a level heart and straight intent; he who is loyal treads only the correct path—as with Xuan's nature, from first to last it can be trusted; your servant prays Your Majesty will pardon Xuan's former faults, allow him to renew himself, raise him to the ministry, and charge his later effect.
proposals.after: As for the pure, the heart is level and the intent straight; the loyal treads only the correct path—as with Xuan's nature, from first to last it can be trusted; your servant prays Your Majesty will pardon Xuan's former faults, allow him to renew himself, raise him to the ministry, and charge his later effect.
proposals.reason: The argument contrasts the pure and the loyal; rendering 失清者 as “he who loses purity” reverses the eulogy of Lou Xuan’s constancy.

proposals.before: Sun Hao, nursing a grudge against Lou Xuan's name, sent him and his son Lou Ju to General Zhang Yi in Jiao with orders to earn merit in war, while secretly instructing Zhang Yi to murder them.
proposals.after: Sun Hao, taking account of Lou Xuan's reputation, again transferred Lou Xuan and his son Lou Ju, handing them to General Zhang Yi in Jiaozhi with orders to prove themselves in battle, while secretly instructing Zhang Yi to kill them.
proposals.reason: 話玄名聲 means taking account of Xuan's reputation, not necessarily nursing a grudge against his name; 復徙 marks another transfer omitted in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: What the Jiangbiao zhuan says is longer in accord with principle.
proposals.after: What the Jiangbiao zhuan says is superior in accord with principle.
proposals.reason: 於理為長 means the account is stronger or preferable in reason, not that it is longer.

proposals.before: Under Sun Hao he became left master of ceremonies, then director of the secretariat, while serving as grand tutor to the heir apparent.
proposals.after: Under Sun Hao he became left army supervisor, then director of the secretariat, while serving as grand tutor to the heir apparent.
proposals.reason: 左典軍 is a military supervisor of the army, not master of ceremonies.

proposals.before: In Sun Hao's time he entered as left master of ceremonies, was transferred to director of the secretariat, and concurrently held grand tutor to the heir apparent.
proposals.after: In Sun Hao's time he entered as left army supervisor, was transferred to director of the secretariat, and concurrently held grand tutor to the heir apparent.
proposals.reason: 左典軍 is a military office (left dianjun), mistranslated as master of ceremonies.

proposals.before: Welcome the long-excluded, hear blunt truth, honor your father's work—then the realm may heal.
proposals.after: If men of that sort are not employed again, broadly advance the long-stagnant, accept blunt speech, and honor the former enterprise, then great transformation will spread and Heaven and men will have their hopes fulfilled.
proposals.reason: The opening 如是之輩一勿/匆復用 is omitted; the sentence first demands that sycophants not be used again.

proposals.before: He died at sixty in the second year of Taixing (321).
proposals.after: He died at sixty in the second year of Taixing (319).
proposals.reason: 太興二年 of Jin Emperor Yuan is AD 319, not 321.

proposals.before: It is no art of war like Sun Wu's.
proposals.after: It is no art of war like that of Sun and Wu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 孫、吳 names the paired military authorities; the idiomatic line keeps only Sun Wu.

proposals.before: When Prince Yuan was general who guards the east, he requested Xun as army marshal; when the Prince became Prince of Jin, he made Xun director of the secretariat—he firmly declined and would not accept, was transferred to grand master of ceremonies, concurrently grand tutor to the heir apparent.
proposals.after: When Emperor Yuan was general who guards the east, he requested Xun as army marshal; when the Prince became Prince of Jin, he made Xun director of the secretariat—he firmly declined and would not accept, was transferred to grand master of ceremonies, concurrently grand tutor to the heir apparent.
proposals.reason: 元皇帝 is the posthumous emperor title Emperor Yuan, not Prince Yuan.

proposals.before: Sun Liang had Zhuge Ke name him grand astrologer for the Book of Wu; under Sun Xun he was gentleman of the secretariat and chief erudit.
proposals.after: When Sun Liang took the throne, Zhuge Ke as regent recommended Yao as grand astrologer to compile the Book of Wu; Hua He, Xue Ying, and others all took part. When Sun Xiu acceded, Yao became gentleman of the secretariat and libationer of the erudits.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits Hua He and Xue Ying, renders Sun Xiu as Sun Xun, and abridges the office 博士祭酒.

proposals.before: When Sun Liang ascended the throne, Zhuge Ke governed and memorialized Yao as grand astrologer to compose the Book of Wu; Hua He, Xue Ying, and others all joined in the same work; when Sun Xun mounted the steps, he was gentleman of the secretariat and libationer of erudits.
proposals.after: When Sun Liang ascended the throne, Zhuge Ke governed and memorialized Yao as grand astrologer to compose the Book of Wu; Hua He, Xue Ying, and others all joined in the same work; when Sun Xiu mounted the steps, he was gentleman of the secretariat and libationer of erudits.
proposals.reason: 孫休 is Sun Xiu, not Sun Xun.

proposals.before: Sun Xun ordered him to collate the imperial library on Liu Xiang's model.
proposals.after: Sun Xiu ordered him to collate the imperial library on Liu Xiang's model.
proposals.reason: The silent subject is Sun Xiu (孫休), wrongly named Sun Xun.

proposals.before: He wished Wei Yao to lecture the throne, but Zhang Bu, the favorite general, blocked it, fearing a scholar would lecture Sun Xun on moral history.
proposals.after: He wished Wei Yao to lecture the throne, but Zhang Bu, the favorite general, blocked it, fearing a scholar would lecture Sun Xiu on moral history.
proposals.reason: 休 is Sun Xiu, not Sun Xun.

proposals.before: He also wished to extend Yao as lecturer-in-waiting, but General of the Left Zhang Bu was a near attendant, favored and doted on, his deeds many times stained; he feared Yao as lecturer, a Confucian gentleman, and moreover by nature precise, feared he would use past and present to warn Xun's intent—therefore he firmly contended that it could not be done.
proposals.after: He also wished to extend Yao as lecturer-in-waiting, but General of the Left Zhang Bu was a near attendant, favored and doted on, his deeds many times stained; he feared Yao as lecturer, a Confucian gentleman, and moreover by nature precise, feared he would use past and present to warn Xiu's intent—therefore he firmly contended that it could not be done.
proposals.reason: 休's given name is Xiu, not Xun.

proposals.before: Sun Xun came to hate Zhang Bu—the story is told in Sun Xun's biography.
proposals.after: Sun Xiu came to hate Zhang Bu—the story is told in Sun Xiu's biography.
proposals.reason: The biography cited is that of Sun Xiu.

proposals.before: Xun deeply hated Bu—the words are in the biography of Xun.
proposals.after: Xiu deeply hated Bu—the words are in the biography of Xiu.
proposals.reason: 休 is Xiu, not Xun.

proposals.before: Moreover Hao wished to make a annals for his father He; Yao insisted that because He did not ascend the imperial seat, it ought to be titled biography.
proposals.after: Moreover Hao wished to make annals for his father He; Yao insisted that because He did not ascend the imperial seat, it ought to be titled biography.
proposals.reason: English article error: 'a annals' should be 'annals'.

proposals.before: Yao by nature drank no more than two sheng of wine; at first when treated with special courtesy, they often reduced the measure for him, or secretly bestowed tea for herbs in place of wine; when favor waned, he met more forced pressure, and that was always taken as a crime.
proposals.after: Yao by nature drank no more than two sheng of wine; at first when treated with special courtesy, they often reduced the measure for him, or secretly bestowed tea in place of wine; when favor waned, he met more forced pressure, and that was always taken as a crime.
proposals.reason: 茶荈 is tea, not tea for herbs.

proposals.before: Ban Gu's Han shu towers over Liu Zhen's Han ji—the latter's biographies are poor stuff.
proposals.after: Ban Gu's Han shu towers over the Han ji of Liu Zhen, Liu Yi, and others—the latter's biographies are poor stuff.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops Liu Yi and the plural others.

proposals.before: At first he was magistrate of Shangyu and commandant of curved agriculture, entered by literary learning as gentleman of the secret archive, was promoted secretariat aide.
proposals.after: At first he was magistrate of Shangyu and commandant of agriculture, entered by literary learning as gentleman of the secret archive, was promoted secretariat aide.
proposals.reason: 曲農都尉 is the agricultural commandant; rendering 曲 as 'curved' makes a mechanical office name that obscures the post.

proposals.before: In the second year of Baoding Sun Hao raised a new palace on a vast plan, inlaid with jade and pearl at ruinous cost.
proposals.after: In the second year of Baoding, Sun Hao raised a new palace on a vast plan, inlaid with jade and pearl at ruinous cost.
proposals.reason: Missing pause fuses the reign title Baoding with the personal name Sun Hao into a spurious compound.

proposals.before: Your servant, though lowest foolish, does not know the great norm, privately takes affairs of the bag-time and measures the present situation.
proposals.after: Your servant, though lowest foolish, does not know the great norm, privately takes affairs of former times and measures the present situation.
proposals.reason: 囊時 here is the common 'former times' (曩時), not a bag.

proposals.before: Jia Yi feared young princes and idle tutors—no Yao could govern so.
proposals.after: Jia Yi said that within a few more years the princes would be in their prime and Han's tutors and chancellors would retire claiming illness—if one tried to govern thus, even Yao and Shun could not keep the peace.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 舜 and flattens Jia Yi's quoted warning about princes and idle tutors.

proposals.before: These halls were built by your father.
proposals.after: These halls were built by the late emperor.
proposals.reason: 先帝 is the previous emperor, not Sun Hao's father; Sun Hao's father was never the reigning emperor who built the palaces.

proposals.before: If stores fail when the north strikes, not even Zhou Gong could save you.
proposals.after: If above and below are exhausted and canal transport fails while the northern enemy violates the border, even if Zhou and Shao were born again and Liang and Ping returned, they could not plan for Your Majesty—this is clear.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops Shao, Liang, Ping, and Your Majesty, collapsing four named exemplars and the throne address into Zhou Gong alone.

proposals.before: That is the first cure for want and the true way to enrich the state—even Guan Zhong could not improve it.
proposals.after: This is the highest task of relieving want and the root enterprise of enriching the state; were Guan and Yan born again, they could not change this.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits Yan, who is paired with Guan in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Sun Hao, citing Hua He's age, ordered him to draft on straw—Hua He refused.
proposals.after: Sun Hao, citing Hua He's age, ordered him to compose a draft memorial; Hua He did not dare.
proposals.reason: Draft-memorial cao-biao is not writing on straw; bu-gan is did not dare rather than refused.

proposals.before: Hao, because He was old in years, ordered him to draft the memorial on grass; He did not dare.
proposals.after: Hao, because He was old in years, ordered him to draft a memorial; He did not dare.
proposals.reason: Cao-biao means to draft a memorial; grass mistranslates cao as a writing surface.

proposals.before: I, Hua He, dust and grass—
proposals.after: I, Hua He, a petty clerk, am mere dust and weeds, ordinary and mean.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 小臣 and 凡庸 and truncates the self-abasement that the Chinese and literal both keep.

proposals.before: He Shao was austere and acute;
proposals.after: He Shao set his will high and pure, and his handling of topics was clear and essential.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic compresses 厲志高潔，機理清要 into unrelated 'austere and acute,' losing will, purity, and topical clarity present in the Chinese.

decisions.reason: 俱為 marks that Wang Fan, He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si jointly received 散騎中常侍; the original’s “became all attendant” is ungrammatical and invents a title.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 與賀邵、薛瑩、虞汜俱為散騎中常侍

decisions.reason: 謂蕃自輕 is the charge that Fan held Wan Yu cheap, not that Fan belittled himself; 挾侵 is nursing a grudge, not “bearing encroachment.”
數譖毀蕃 is repeated slander and defamation; the Chinese does not say Chen Sheng already ruined Fan.
Parallel 忠者 and the eulogy of Lou Xuan’s 清忠 show the subject is the pure man, not one who loses purity. CText reads 夫清者; 失 is a graphic slip for 夫.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 失清者則心平而意直，忠者惟正道而履之

decisions.after: Sun Hao, resenting Lou Xuan's reputation, again transferred Lou Xuan and his son Lou Ju, handing them to General Zhang Yi in Jiaozhi with orders to prove themselves in battle, while secretly instructing Zhang Yi to kill them.
decisions.reason: The original omits 復徙 and shortens 交阯, which the proposal restores, but 話玄名聲 is a weak reading: CText has 皓疾玄名聲, which supports resentment rather than merely “taking account.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皓話玄名聲，復徙玄及子據，付交阯將張奕

decisions.reason: 於理為長 means the Jiangbiao zhuan account is the stronger or preferable in reason, not that it is longer.
左典軍 is a military post (left army supervisor), not master of ceremonies.
左典軍 is left army supervisor, mistranslated as master of ceremonies.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 入為左典軍，遷中書令，領太子太傅

decisions.after: If men of that sort are not employed again, broadly advance the long-stagnant, accept blunt speech, reverently follow Heaven's direction, and honor the former enterprise, then great transformation will spread and Heaven and men will have their hopes fulfilled.
decisions.reason: The original omits 如是之輩，一匆復用, which the proposal restores, but it still drops 祗承乾指, which the Chinese pairs with 敬奉先業.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 如是之輩，一匆復用，廣延淹滯，容受直辭，祗承乾指，敬奉先業

decisions.reason: 太興二年 of Jin Emperor Yuan is AD 319; 321 would be 太興四年.
孫、吳 names the paired authorities Sun and Wu, not a single “Sun Wu.”
元皇帝 is the posthumous imperial title Emperor Yuan, not Prince Yuan.
The original omits 華核、薛瑩, names 孫休 as Sun Xun, and abridges 博士祭酒; the replacement restores all three.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 華核、薛瑩等皆與參同，孫休踐阼，為中書郎、博士祭酒

decisions.reason: 孫休 is Sun Xiu, not Sun Xun.
The silent subject of 命曜 is Sun Xiu from 孫休踐阼, not Sun Xun.
休意 is Sun Xiu’s mind, not Sun Xun’s.
休’s given name is Xiu, not Xun.
《休傳》 is the biography of Sun Xiu.
休 is Xiu, not Xun, both as agent and in 《休傳》.
作紀 is “make annals”; the original’s “a annals” is an English article error, not a Chinese meaning.
茶荈 is tea (tea leaves), not “tea for herbs.”
劉珍，劉毅等 names Liu Zhen, Liu Yi, and others as compilers of the Han ji; the original drops Liu Yi and the plural 等.
Rendering 曲 as “curved” invents a mechanical office name. CText reads the standard post 典農都尉, agricultural commandant.
The original already takes 實鼎二年 as the date and 皓 as Sun Hao; adding a comma is punctuation only and does not correct meaning.
囊時 is 曩時 “former times,” not “bag-time.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 竊以囊時之事，揆今之勢

decisions.reason: The quotation names 堯、舜 and warns that princes would be in their prime while tutors retired claiming illness; the original drops Shun and flattens the warning.
先帝 is the late emperor, not “your father.” Sun Hao’s father never reigned as the emperor who built these halls.
周、召更生，良、平復出 names four exemplars plus 陛下; collapsing them into Zhou Gong alone omits Shao, Liang, Ping, and the throne address.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 使周、召更生，良、平復出，不能為陛下計明矣

decisions.reason: 管、晏復生 pairs Guan with Yan; the original keeps only Guan Zhong.
草表 is to draft a memorial, not write on straw; 不敢 is “did not dare,” not a firm refusal.
草表 means draft a memorial; 草 is not a writing surface of grass.
咨核小臣，草芥凡庸 keeps 小臣 and 凡庸 in the self-abasement; the original truncates both.
厲志高潔，機理清要 is setting the will high and pure and handling topics with clear essentials, not merely “austere and acute.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 賀邵厲志高潔，機理清要
